scope: Open review of hepatopulmonary syndrome as a liver-disease complication with intrapulmonary vascular dilatations, shunting, and liver transplantation as the disease-modifying treatment.

keyRecommendations.text: HPS is a pulmonary complication of liver disease that adversely affects prognosis.
It is characterised by intrapulmonary vascular dilatations and shunts causing impaired gas exchange.
Liver transplantation is the only therapeutic option and generally reverses HPS. Outcomes improved after the MELD standard-exception policy.

clinicalBottomLine: Recognise HPS as gas-exchange failure from intrapulmonary vascular dilatations in liver disease. Liver transplantation is the treatment that generally reverses it.
notableCaveats: The stored hepatitis B guidance is a different disease and was not used. Platypnoea is not stated in the sentences used here.
